note: 目标 the-lovers-painting 全正文全部FAQ核读。原句：Rene Magritte's The Lovers is not one painting but two: a couple kissing through white cloth at MoMA in New York, and a second version showing the couple facing forward at the National Gallery of Australia in Canberra, both painted in Paris in 1928 and both close to 54 by 73 centimetres. Nearly every account of the veiled faces repeats the same explanation, that as a boy Magritte watched his drowned mother's body pulled from the River Sambre with her nightgown wrapped around her face. Wikipedia's entry on Magritte states that later research discredited that eyewitness story, and a 2018 review in the New York Review of Books calls it a family legend, now discredited. Magritte was thirteen when his mother died on 24 February 1912, not fourteen as some retellings claim, and his own description of the day left the riverbank out entirely: In 1912, his mother Regina is tired of life. She throws herself into the Sambre.。源当前句：A single painted subject splitting into two separate, differently documented objects happens elsewhere in this period too: [Rene Magritte painted The Lovers twice in Paris in 1928, and the two canvases, now held on opposite sides of the world, carry ownership records that look nothing alike](/the-lovers-painting/).。全读1928Paris两独立canvas/NYMoMA与CanberraNGA，各provenance和母亲eyewitnesslegend不可靠及全FAQ。新原桥接只同subject多object并不同ownership，目标开篇确有两机构；不推一幅复制另一幅。
